explanation: Tax Court cites Seltzer only for the summary-judgment standard (doubts resolved against movant). Lyon v. Barrett overruled Seltzer's substantive legal-malpractice holding (own knowledge; no excerpt), a different point, so limb 1 fails.

Lee cites Fisher and Holmes as support that a larceny verdict must declare value and reverses on it; Griffith (1913) had overruled both outright on that verdict-value rule (own knowledge; no excerpt). No mention of Griffith.

Alaska court adopts the per se reversal rule for jury separation, citing D'Antonio and 'See' Panczko as authority; Arciniega had overruled both on that rule 18 days earlier. No negative history noted; unrelated litigation.

Oliver relies on Haehlen for the nuisance rule that courts cannot set aesthetic standards absent legislation; Varney appears only as the source Haehlen quoted. Metromedia overruled Varney on police-power regulation for aesthetics, a different point.

Messersmith cites the 1903 Harris v. Stearns opinion as authority that a clear tax receipt is conclusive of prior taxes paid; that opinion's affirmance was overruled and reversed on rehearing in 1906 (negated as a whole). No history noted; different litigation.

Florida court cites Montgomery v. Anderson, with parenthetical, as authority upholding a 30 percent vote requirement against equal-protection attack; North Dakota had overruled it on that validity point by 1918 (own knowledge; no excerpt). No acknowledgment.

Louisiana court cites Holmes for the conduct standard warranting punitive damages for unpaid maintenance and cure and applies it; Guevara (en banc 1995) overruled Holmes on availability of such punitive damages. Guevara not mentioned.
